query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive approach that integrates atomic-scale descriptors of chemical disorder (e.g. quantified force‐constant fluctuations) with mesoscale structural metrics (such as controlled pore characteristics or nanostructural features) will identify high-entropy alloys with ultra-low phonon thermal conductivity with at least 20% higher predictive accuracy than models based solely on simplified supercell or binary alloy descriptors.
generation.material_initial_state: A fully dense, single-phase high-entropy alloy (e.g. an equiatomic five-element solid solution such as FeCoCrMnNi without engineered porosity) prepared by conventional synthesis methods.
generation.intervention: Apply the new predictive approach (e.g. an ML-enhanced DFT framework that incorporates multi-scale features including force-constant fluctuations and local chemical variance) to screen candidate HEA compositions for targeted ultra-low lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.conditions: Measurements are performed at room temperature under ambient pressure, with subsequent phonon dispersion and thermal conductivity characterization by inelastic neutron/X-ray scattering and laser flash analysis.
generation.structural_mediator: The magnitude of lattice distortions – captured via atomic-level force-constant fluctuation metrics (20–50% variations) and local chemical fluctuation indicators – mediates enhanced phonon scattering.
generation.mechanism: Increased chemical disorder and lattice distortion generate a broadened distribution of local bonding environments. This, when coupled with effective mesoscale features (if present), reduces the phonon mean free path by intensifying phonon scattering, thereby lowering the lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: HEAs predicted by the integrated multi-scale model will exhibit lattice thermal conductivity values comparable to or lower than 0.4 W/(m·K) (as seen in some high-entropy thermoelectric systems) and show a demonstrably shorter phonon mean free path than alloys selected by conventional models.
generation.baseline: Existing predictive models built on simplified supercells or binary alloy analogues that do not incorporate the full spectrum of chemical disorder and mesoscale structural features.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for single-phase high-entropy alloys (with ≥5 principal elements) where the electron contribution to thermal conductivity is minimal, and the material remains structurally stable without phase separation or significant porosity beyond designed features.
generation.uncertainty: The proposal extends findings from studies showing measurable force-constant fluctuations in FeCoCrMnNi (PMC9726824::web::014) and low κ predictions in PbSnTeSe (PMC9822225::web::004) to a multi-scale predictive model in dense HEAs. Uncertainty remains in the exact magnitude of improved predictive accuracy and the effect of simulation limitations (e.g. supercell size) when generalizing to HEAs with complex chemistries, as highlighted by conflicting observations in the same FeCoCrMnNi system (PMC9726824::web::021).

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of high-entropy alloys that the predictive approach identifies as having ultra-low lattice thermal conductivity. Characterize these alloys using inelastic neutron/X-ray scattering to quantify phonon dispersions and measure the bulk lattice thermal conductivity via laser flash analysis. In parallel, apply conventional predictive models to select a control set of HEAs.
measurements: Quantitative determination of lattice thermal conductivity (W/(m·K))
Phonon mean free path and dispersion curves from scattering experiments
Comparison of predicted versus measured force-constant fluctuation metrics
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs selected by the new predictive approach do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction (≥20% improvement) in lattice thermal conductivity and correspondingly lower phonon mean free paths compared to those chosen by conventional models, then the hypothesis that the integrated multi-scale predictive method is superior will be falsified.
